summary: Bonsai Radio is a cyberpunk-themed Progressive Web App (PWA) for streaming playlist-based "radio" audio from an Internet Computer (Motoko) backend. Public users can browse playlists, play tracks in sequence, increment per-track play counts, and participate in listener-count sessions. Authenticated DJs (Internet Identity + admin role) get a command-center dashboard to manage a media library (upload/edit/delete/search), build playlists (from uploads or the library), and curate audio-reactive background visuals via a GIF gallery and tunable overlay settings. AirPlay support is being integrated for streaming audio to AirPlay-enabled devices.

existing_features.title: Public playlist browsing
existing_features.description: Provides a public backend query (getPlaylists) and frontend query hook (useGetPlaylists) to fetch and display available playlists and their tracks without authentication, with periodic polling for freshness.

existing_features.title: Radio-style streaming player
existing_features.description: Public player UI to select a playlist/channel, play/pause audio, display now-playing metadata, auto-advance tracks on ended, and show per-track play counts.

existing_features.title: Play count tracking
existing_features.description: On track end, the frontend calls a public mutation to increment a track’s playCount inside the selected playlist, and refreshes playlist data via React Query invalidation.

existing_features.title: Listener count and sessions
existing_features.description: Backend tracks active listener sessions and exposes listenerCount publicly; frontend starts a session when playback begins (RadioPlayer) and stops it on unmount, while polling and displaying current listener count.

existing_features.title: Stream stability monitoring and adaptive retry
existing_features.description: Players detect buffering/error states (waiting/progress/error events), show a StreamStabilityIndicator, and attempt exponential-backoff retries with jitter and fade-in on recovery.

existing_features.title: Audio analysis for reactive UI
existing_features.description: Analyzes playing audio via Web Audio API (AnalyserNode) to compute volume, frequency bands, bass kick detection, and spectral centroid, with adaptive throttling for mobile/hidden tabs.

existing_features.title: Audio-reactive cyberpunk background visuals
existing_features.description: Renders an animated cyberpunk wallpaper with parallax and canvas-based particles/flares/light beams; intensity reacts to audio analysis data and adapts frame rate for performance.

existing_features.title: Background GIF overlay during playback
existing_features.description: Displays a semi-transparent GIF overlay when playing; selects random GIF on track change (if enabled) with fade transitions and backend-configurable transparency/fade/intensity.

existing_features.title: DJ authentication via Internet Identity
existing_features.description: Implements Internet Identity login/logout, session restoration, and a DJAuthModal UX; authenticated identity is used to create an authorized actor and check admin status before showing DJ tools.

existing_features.title: Role-based access control (admin/user/guest)
existing_features.description: Backend enforces permissions for DJ-only operations (media library, playlist writes, GIF management). Access control is initialized via secret token; only admins can assign roles or initialize default GIFs.

existing_features.title: DJ dashboard and control panel
existing_features.description: Admin-only dashboard with stats and a tabbed control panel (create playlists, view playlists, media library, embedded player, background visuals), with active tab persisted to localStorage.

existing_features.title: Media library management (DJ)
existing_features.description: DJ-only media library supports upload (ExternalBlob), list, sort, search, edit metadata, and delete tracks; UI includes table view, search, sorting, and status badges.

existing_features.title: Batch operations for tracks
existing_features.description: Media library supports multi-select with batch actions: add one/many tracks to one/many playlists and batch edit metadata fields via BatchEditTrackDialog.

existing_features.title: Playlist management (DJ)
existing_features.description: DJ-only mutations to create playlists from uploaded files, create playlists from media library selections, and add single/multiple library tracks to existing playlists; frontend forms and dialogs cover these flows.

existing_features.title: Background visuals administration (DJ)
existing_features.description: DJ UI to upload/delete background GIFs, preview visuals, and update settings (transparency, fade duration, animation intensity, randomization). Includes client-side queuing behavior for “upload system not ready” errors.

existing_features.title: Default background GIF seeding
existing_features.description: On first admin session, the frontend can seed the backend with a default set of GIFs (from bundled assets) if the backend collection is empty.

existing_features.title: PWA installability and theming
existing_features.description: Includes manifest.json, theme colors, icons, and meta tags to support installation as a standalone Progressive Web App with Bonsai Radio branding.

existing_features.title: Caffeine blob storage integration utilities
existing_features.description: Backend includes storage mixin endpoints for gateway principal updates, dead-blob listing and confirmation, cashier refill, and certificate creation to support ExternalBlob upload lifecycle.

existing_features.title: User profile storage (backend)
existing_features.description: Backend supports saving and retrieving user profiles for authenticated users (user role), with admin override for viewing other profiles; no frontend UI is shown in provided files.

existing_features.title: Improve AirPlay runtime detection so the app correctly reflects when AirPlay is actually available vs unavailable, by using the `webkitplaybacktargetavailabilitychanged` event payload to set `isAvailable` true/false (not always true), and keep `isConnected` synchronized with `webkitCurrentPlaybackTargetIsWireless` on initial load and on change.

When the AirPlay route changes (connect/disconnect), automatically recover playback by reloading the current audio source and resuming playback if the user was playing, while preserving the intended track and approximate playback position when possible.

Reduce AirPlay buffering stalls by adjusting the player’s buffering/retry strategy specifically when AirPlay is connected (e.g., more conservative thresholding and/or quicker recovery actions on repeated `waiting`/low-buffer conditions), without regressing non-AirPlay playback.

Add clear, English user-facing messaging in the player UI when AirPlay is connected but audio is not successfully playing (e.g., extended buffering or repeated playback failures), including a one-click action to retry/reconnect AirPlay playback (e.g., “Retry AirPlay” or “Reconnect”).

new_feature_requests.summary: Integrate Apple AirPlay support for streaming audio to AirPlay-enabled devices from the web app (including optional device-selection UI).
Fix AirPlay playback reliability: reduce buffering and ensure audio actually routes to the AirPlay device during playback.

architectural_notes: Frontend is React + TypeScript using @tanstack/react-query for all backend interactions (queries, mutations, cache invalidation, periodic polling).
Internet Identity authentication is encapsulated in a provider hook (AuthClient), exposing identity/login/logout and login status to the app.
Canister actor creation is centralized in a useActor hook; actor is recreated per identity and triggers downstream query invalidation/refetch.
Backend is a single Motoko actor using in-memory Map structures for playlists, media library, listener sessions, background GIFs/settings, and user profiles (no stable persistence shown).
Role-based access control is implemented via an AccessControl module and included as a mixin; first valid caller with an admin token becomes admin; others become users/guests.
Blob uploads are handled via a Caffeine storage mixin (ExternalBlob) with gateway authorization updates, blob lifecycle queries, and cashier refill hooks.
UI uses TailwindCSS + shadcn/ui components with extensive custom neon animations and responsive layouts.
Audio-reactive visuals are driven by a Web Audio API analyser hook (FFT/bands/kick detection), influencing background canvas effects and UI glow styles.
App includes a dual-mode UX: public RadioPlayer and DJDashboard with tabbed tools and localStorage persistence for active tab.
Default background GIFs are seeded on first admin session by sending asset URLs to the backend initialization method.
known_issues: Track identity is effectively the track title throughout (mediaLibrary Map key, update/delete operations, playlist add operations), making IDs non-unique and prone to collisions/overwrites.
Renaming a track title via updateTrackMetadata/updateTracksMetadata does not migrate the Map key; title changes can desync lookup IDs and stored values.
Volume normalization toggles reference gainNodeRef, but no GainNode is created/connected in the players; normalization likely has no effect.
Listener sessions are keyed by caller Principal; anonymous users share the anonymous principal, so listener counts may be inaccurate for unauthenticated listeners.
startListenerSession traps if a session already exists; refresh/reconnect flows can yield repeated "already active" errors unless stopListenerSession runs successfully.
Public getBackgroundGifs has no pagination/limits and returns full blobs array; large GIF collections could impact performance/bandwidth.
AccessControl.getUserRole traps for unregistered principals; behavior depends on clients always calling _initializeAccessControlWithSecret after authentication.
Backend state is in-memory only in the provided code; playlists/media library/background GIFs likely reset on canister upgrade unless stable storage exists elsewhere.
Caffeine blob storage uploads can fail with `403 - Owner does not have an account with the cashier`, blocking track/GIF uploads until the canister is activated/registered with the storage cashier.
AirPlay may connect to a device but playback buffers heavily and/or produces no audio output through the AirPlay route (routing/compatibility issue in current AirPlay integration).
